title: Use potential-dependent solenoidal gauges without claiming cancellation of constitutive work
statement: AtmeanI,u=x1+f,v=x2+g,smooth one-periodicLambda gives tau_Lambda=Lambda(u)RDu periodic/solenoidal with mean(meanLambda)e2. Thus integralLambda(u)detD(u,v)=meanLambda; at conditional row minimizer with stresss, integralLambda(u)s.Du=meanLambda integral s.Du. No invertibleu/regularfoliation required. Any invertible real mean can use constant left rotation firstmeanrow(a,0),Lambda0(u/a),unchangedsource lattice. But constitutive lambda(F) depends on GRADIENT: integral[lambda(F)-Lambda(u)]RDu.Dg=integral lambda(F)RDu.Dg. The subtracted part is exactly zero solenoidal-gradient pairing. Gauge does not pay the missing Euler work or universal original comparison.
